title: Skipped steps in the shared progress stepper (transfer)
prompt: Onboarding lets people skip checklist items, but `OnboardingProgress` shows a skipped item with a check mark as if it were done. Designers want skipped steps to get a muted indicator with a dash (–) instead of the check or number; everything else about the stepper, including the line after each step, stays exactly as it is. `ProgressSteps` (`src/components/progress-steps.tsx`) is shared with `TaskStatusSteps`, which must look exactly the same as today. Keep the stepper code easy to change.

criteria.text: The step-state decision (complete/current/upcoming, plus skipped) is computed once by a named pure function at module scope in `progress-steps.tsx` (e.g. `getStepState(step, currentStep, skipped)` returning a string-literal union), or once per step boundary and shared through the step context. ProgressStep, ProgressStepIndicator, and ProgressStepConnector no longer each repeat raw `step < currentStep` / `step === currentStep` comparisons; the nested ternary in ProgressStep is gone. The connector may use the position-based state (e.g. the same helper without the skipped input, or a separate position value) as long as the comparison logic itself is written once.

`src/components/progress-steps.tsx` stays generic: it imports nothing from `src/features/*` and knows nothing about onboarding items or task statuses; skipped arrives as a generic per-step input (e.g. a `skipped` boolean on ProgressStep or a step state supplied by the consumer). The step-state helper lives in the family file (module-private), not in `src/lib`, a `helpers.ts`, or a feature folder.

Connector appearance is unchanged for skipped steps: the line after a skipped step that lies before the current step is still the primary color, exactly as before. A solution that derives the connector color from a state value where skipped no longer counts as complete (so the line turns gray) is a fail. Last-step connector still returns null.

OnboardingProgress passes each item's `skipped` to its step, and skipped steps render a muted indicator containing a dash instead of the check or number. Non-skipped steps keep their previous classes, icon/number, data-state, and aria-current. The `firstOpenIndex` logic for currentStep is unchanged.

In `TaskStatusSteps`, the let/if/else chain mapping status to the current step is replaced with simpler control flow, ideally a typed `Record<TaskStatus, number>` lookup constant (or a small named function) kept in the tasks feature file, and `done` still maps past the last index (3 / stepLabels.length) so every step renders complete. Mapping done to 2 is a fail. Its rationale comment survives at the mapping.

The onboarding current-step derivation and the task status mapping stay in their own features; they are not merged into one shared helper or moved into the generic family, since they encode different rules. No feature imports from the other feature.

New helpers are module-private (not added to the family's export list) unless a consumer outside the module uses them. No new hook wraps a pure calculation other than the existing context readers, no useMemo/useCallback added, no new files created for single helpers. Readers like useProgressStep may return the derived state if that is where the decision lives.
Both consumers compile against the updated family and the project typechecks.
